title: FPS game protype in a browser. Couple hours of vibing with gemini 3.
author: marsilainen

replies.author: gastro_psychic
replies.body: Did you have Gemini generate the graphics?

replies.author: marsilainen
replies.body: I made the meshes in blender. Two little textures from nano banana.

replies.author: marsilainen
replies.body: Just manual modeling and then importing the models to the project. I started experimenting with using hitem3d for the mesh generation.

replies.author: odragora
replies.body: It really fits the old-school style, looks great!

comments.author: Brave-History-6502
comments.body: reminds me of unreal tournament or one of those older FPS games

replies.author: gastro_psychic
replies.body: I loved playing UT as a kid.

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body: same, the graphics were so good for the time haha

comments.author: No_You3985
comments.body: Is it possible for Gemini 3 to use unreal engine 5? It would be really cool

comments.author: windyx
comments.body: Now tell it to make a game that it doesn't know about and see how well it figures out movement / etc. you're asking it to replicate code that was in the training set.

replies.author: marsilainen
replies.body: Yeah i'm not expecting much creativity out of these. I already had to be pretty specific on what I want and make this in phases. 3D framework -> basic map -> movement -> tweak movement feeling -> first gun -> back to map features etc... Fun stuff to do on the weekend anyway.

comments.author: WiseOldToad
comments.body:
Just to satisfy my own curiosity -- what's the math behind the gravity/physics here?

Feels a touch floaty and I'm curious if its because gravity is modeled as a constant velocity (rather than exponential)?

Cool stuff though. Coding with AI is a blast.

comments.author: ZHName
comments.body: Hours will be seconds in next 36 months.
